citations.source: 李學勤主編《字源》；白于藍撰「上」條
citations.field: 上部 / 上 / 字形與用例；PDF p.14, printed p.2
citations.text: The entry calls 上 an indicative graph. It says the oracle forms place a short horizontal mark above a longer line to indicate the upper position; the bronze form continues this pattern. Spring-and-Autumn forms include an added vertical stroke, which the entry identifies as the basis of the clerical form. Warring States forms vary, including decorative strokes, omission of the upper short line, and forms with 是 or 止 added as meaning determinatives, yielding compounds analyzed as 从是或止、上声. The entry says the original meaning was spatial, opposite 下, and reports extensions to high places, heaven, and ruler. The historical glyph sequence and prose were checked directly against the scan; the next page begins the 帝 entry, confirming this passage ends on p.14.
